blocks.content: Course: Make Your Website Interactive with JavaScript
When you build something like a slider, the page needs to keep track of one key piece of information.
That piece of information is called state.
State is simply a value stored in your code that represents the current condition of the UI.
In a slider, we usually store it in a variable like this:
This variable becomes the source of truth. Every time the user clicks Next or Previous, we update this number. Then we update the UI to match it.
State changes first. The interface reflects that change.
Next, you'll see a small runnable example that makes this pattern concrete.
